66.solution: Polyester fibres such as terylene are blended with wool to make terywool. Bristles of brushes are made from nylon. Orlon is polyacrylonitrile, not a polyester. Hence the answer is D.

69.solution: Barium sulphate is insoluble in water and in stomach acid, so it is not absorbed and is not toxic. It is opaque to X-rays, so it outlines the intestine. Soluble barium salts are poisonous. Hence the answer is B.

72.solution:
**Note:** As printed none of the four compounds is chiral. The answer shown follows the paper's key, (D).

A chiral molecule has a carbon bonded to four different groups. In 2-chloropropane C2 carries two \(\text{CH}_3\) groups. In 2-chloro-2-methylbutane (option C names the same compound) C2 carries two \(\text{CH}_3\) groups. In 3-chloropentane C3 carries two \(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\) groups. None of the four molecules is chiral.

76.solution: A thermosetting polymer forms a cross-linked network on heating and cannot be remoulded. Urea formaldehyde resin is such a polymer. Polystyrene is a thermoplastic, and polyesters and polyamides used as fibres are linear thermoplastics. Hence the answer is A.

85.solution: Ethyl phenyl ketone is \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COC}_2\text{H}_5\). Hydrazine gives the hydrazone A. Heating A with KOH in ethylene glycol is the Wolff-Kishner reduction, which turns \(\text{C=O}\) into \(\text{CH}_2\). B is \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3\), n-propylbenzene. Hence the answer is C.

88.solution: Cl on the ring is deactivating but ortho, para directing. Chlorination with \(\text{Cl}_2\) and anhydrous \(\text{FeCl}_3\) gives o- and p-dichlorobenzene. The para isomer is the major product because the ortho position is crowded. Hence the answer is D.
